name: copilot-cache-keeper
description: Warns before a Copilot chat's prompt cache expires; keep it warm or write a handoff summary.

commands.title: Cache Keeper: Manage chats in this window
Cache Keeper: Write handoff summary now

cacheKeeper.warnSeconds.description: Warn this many seconds before the cache expires.

enumDescriptions: Do nothing: the cache expires (after a handoff summary if it is above your summary threshold).
Keep warm once: send one keep-alive before it expires.
Auto keep warm: keep it warm before each expiry, up to the auto keep warm cap.
cacheKeeper.noResponseAction.description: What to do when a warning gets no answer before the cache expires. Either way, warnings for that chat then stop until you write in it again. Applies only to chats active since VS Code started and whose price is known.

cacheKeeper.thresholdCredits.description: Act automatically (handoff summary) only when letting the cache expire would add at least this many credits to the next message, priced from the price sheet Copilot sent for that chat at the chat's current context size. Below it, or when the model's price is unknown, only warn.

cacheKeeper.autoSummary.description: Above the threshold, write a handoff summary if nobody answers the warning.

enumDescriptions: 100%: never spend more than the expiry would have cost
cacheKeeper.autoKeepWarmCapPercent.description: Auto keep warm stops once its keep-alives have cost this share of what letting the cache expire would have added, priced when auto keep warm started. It then writes a handoff summary and lets the cache expire.

cacheKeeper.minCredits.description: Ignore sessions where an expired cache would cost less than this.

cacheKeeper.ttlSeconds.description: Cache lifetime override per model id, in seconds, e.g. {"claude-opus-5.5": 300}. Otherwise learned from Copilot CLI logs, then built-in defaults (Claude 300, Sol 6.1 1800, others 300).

cacheKeeper.keepAliveLeadSeconds.description: Send keep-alives this many seconds before the cache expires (all models). A keep-alive buys a full cache lifetime from when it is sent, so later is cheaper; too late risks missing it.

enumDescriptions: Put the chat where you last typed back into the Chat view; close the other tabs. Right as long as you type in the chat you are looking at.
Just close the tab. If the chat was in the Chat view, the view falls back to the sessions list.
Leave the tab open; nothing is moved or closed.
cacheKeeper.afterSend.description: What to do with the chat tab Cache Keeper opened to send a keep-alive or summary, once the reply is in. (VS Code does not tell extensions which chat the Chat view shows, so only where you last typed is known.)
